proposals.after: Once his schooling was done, he so admired the conduct of Lin Xiangru that he adopted the name Xiangru for himself.

proposals.before: When they were deep in wine, the magistrate stepped forward with a zither and said, “I hear you are fond of this instrument—may I offer you a tune for your pleasure?”
proposals.after: When they were deep in wine, the magistrate stepped forward with a zither and said, “I have heard that Zhangqing is fond of this; I wish to amuse myself with it.”
proposals.reason: 願以自娛 means the magistrate wishes to amuse himself by playing, not to offer Xiangru a tune for Xiangru's pleasure.

decisions.reason: s0005 has only 慕藺相如之為人也; 趙 is absent, so English “of Zhao” invents polity not stated in this sentence, and dropping it restores the Chinese scope.
The quoted speech is 竊聞長卿好之，願以自娛: the magistrate names Zhangqing and says he wishes to amuse himself; “offer you a tune for your pleasure” reverses agent and beneficiary.
